personal.name: Jay Shah
personal.title: Software Engineering Student
personal.intro: I'm a Computer Science student at King's College London, focused on machine learning, data-driven systems, and building reliable software. I enjoy working across the stack and on problems that reward strong quantitative reasoning.

paragraphs: Currently pursuing a BSc in Computer Science at King's College London, where I'm expected to graduate with First Class Honours in May 2026.

My journey in technology began early, starting with Python in Year 6 through Code Club. Since then, I've developed expertise across the full stack, from machine learning algorithms to user interfaces.

I'm particularly drawn to projects that combine technical complexity with real-world impact, whether that's building sentiment analysis tools for financial markets or creating data-driven applications that solve genuine problems.

projects.title: Dissertation: Explainable Regime Discovery in Financial Time Series
projects.description: Designed a dual-track XAI framework applying Vector SHAP and TimeSHAP to an unsupervised LSTM autoencoder trained on 25 years of S&P 500 data. Built a 2-layer stacked LSTM encoder with reverse reconstruction into a 32-dimensional latent space; K-Means with entropy-based model selection and logistic regression soft assignments discovers market regimes unsupervised. Track 1 attributes cluster membership via exact Vector SHAP; Track 2 identifies structurally anomalous market periods via TimeSHAP; faithfulness validated via feature ablation and sanity checks.

projects.title: Quantitative Trading Hackathon (Quantihack) - 2nd Place
projects.description: Sponsored by Anthropic, Jane Street & Optiver. Wheat trading strategy: generated monthly trading signals from annual supply data using satellite images of wheat farms, achieving 17.5% annualised alpha (Sharpe 0.63, -10.4% max drawdown) over a 12-year backtest. Built a correlation-weighted, z-scored composite signal from lagged features, ranking as the top-performing algorithm for multiple days and finishing 2nd overall in the finals.

projects.title: King's Capital - Quantitative Trading Strategies
projects.description: As Head of Quantitative Trading at King's College London's investment society, developed and deployed systematic strategies across equities and commodities. Built an alternative data-driven oil strategy using satellite imagery (inventory shadow analysis) and maritime shipping data. Designed an after-hours earnings momentum strategy and a volatility arbitrage framework selling ATM straddles, forecasting realised volatility via EGARCH, DS3M, GNN-HAR, and CNN-HAR+Ridge with earnings blockers and regime filters. Presented to Deutsche Bank's Quantitative Investment Solutions team (MDs and VPs) and pitched to MCD Capital for a potential £100k allocation.

subprojects.title: Volatility Arbitrage Strategy
subprojects.description: Built a multi-model volatility arbitrage system trading ATM equity straddles across a 20-stock universe. Enters short positions when implied volatility exceeds forecasted realised volatility (with regime and earnings filters), and long in the reverse case. Ensemble of EGARCH, DS³M, GNN-HAR, and HAR-CNN forecasting models. Best model (EGARCH) achieved Sharpe 1.29 and 89% total return over a Jul '20–Dec '24 backtest; DS³M delivered Sharpe 1.02; GNN-HAR and HAR-CNN both ~0.68–0.69. Includes daily delta hedging, earnings blockers, and margin caps.

subprojects.title: GNN-HAR Realised Volatility Forecasting
subprojects.description: Implemented a graph neural network combined with a Heterogeneous Autoregressive (HAR) model to forecast 5-day-ahead realised volatility across 74 S&P 500 stocks. A Graphical LASSO (GLASSO) structure encodes conditional dependencies between stocks as a sparse learned graph, capturing cross-asset volatility spillover alongside each stock's own daily/weekly/monthly RV patterns. Retrained every 21 trading days on a rolling 2-year window using a Quasi-likelihood loss to penalise under-predictions.

subprojects.title: HAR-CNN Realised Volatility Forecasting
subprojects.description: Extended a 2025 paper by encoding 16 HAR-type volatility components across 16 rolling lag windows into a 16×16 "HAR image", then applying a CNN as a feature extractor. The 64-dimensional penultimate layer representations are concatenated with standard HAR predictors and fed into per-ticker Ridge regression heads to produce continuous next-day RV forecasts — adapting the original binary classification model for use in an IV-RV spread trading system.

subprojects.title: DS³M Regime-Switching Volatility Model
subprojects.description: Implemented the Deep Switching State Space Model (DS³M) in PyTorch for volatility forecasting, using a 2-regime (Calm/Stress) discrete latent state and a 4-dimensional continuous latent state. The model separates structural regime shifts from within-regime fluctuations, outperforming EGARCH in capturing nonlinear dynamics and abrupt state changes. Achieved Sharpe 1.02 when used as the forecasting backbone in the vol arb strategy.

subprojects.title: Quantitative Equity Portfolio Management (QEPM)
subprojects.description: Developed a market-neutral long/short equity strategy over the S&P 1500 universe, benchmarked against the S&P 500. Stocks ranked via composite Z-scores (momentum, value, size factors); expected returns from a Fama-French 3-factor model with mean-variance optimisation subject to beta-neutrality, dollar-neutrality, sector neutrality, and a 7% annualised volatility target. Added a regime gate based on an Opportunity Ratio to only deploy capital in alpha-rich environments, achieving 292% final return with 74% alpha. Presented to Deutsche Bank's Quantitative Investment Solutions team (MDs and VPs) and pitched to MCD Capital for a potential £100k allocation.

subprojects.title: Satellite Oil Trading Strategy
subprojects.description: Built an alternative data pipeline using free Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to monitor shadow levels across 97 floating-roof oil storage tanks at Cushing, OK and the US Gulf Coast. Shadow depth proxies oil inventory levels; combined with maritime AIS vessel data tracking international ballast arrivals at 5 Gulf Coast export ports, the dual-signal system generates contrarian WTI futures trades. Achieved Sharpe 0.56 and +152% total return (2018–2025) with an average out-of-sample Sharpe of 0.53 across walk-forward validation.

subprojects.title: After-Hours Earnings Momentum Strategy
subprojects.description: Designed a strategy exploiting post-earnings price continuation by entering positions in the after-hours session immediately following earnings announcements. Entry signals require a meaningful EPS surprise, a minimum after-hours price move, and elevated after-hours volume relative to the 30-day median. Positions held up to 3 days with a trailing stop. Across 227 trades (2021–2026): 63% win rate, Sharpe 0.83, and 4.54x final equity.
